entries.definition: far more than usual or expected
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one member whose excess can flatter, registering a degree far past what was expected as remarkable rather than as a fault.
examples: Elizabeth was chiefly struck with his extraordinary deference for Lady Catherine

entries.definition: far beyond a norm in quantity or amount or degree; to an utmost degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the utmost degree flatly, measuring how far a quantity, amount or degree sits from the norm without ruling on whether that is a fault.

entries.definition: beyond a norm in opinion or actions
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely positional: it sets an opinion or action out past the norm and leaves the verdict to whoever is looking, where *outrageous* is all verdict.

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cool, sizing the overshoot rather than complaining about it as *unreasonable* does.

entries.definition: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hottest word here: the excess is treated as an affront, and the word demands that someone object.
examples: spends an outrageous amount on entertainment

entries.definition: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Marks opinions and actions as standing well past the norm by commitment rather than by accident of degree, and eyes that commitment with reserve.

entries.definition: far more than usual or expected
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sizes an excess by calling it a wrong, so the same far-more-than-expected that *extraordinary* admires becomes something to answer for.

entries.definition: complete or extreme
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Absolute rather than excessive, saying a thing is complete or extreme with nothing softening it, so its force is bleakness rather than blame.

entries.definition: greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and dry, registering a large overshoot as a grumble rather than the protest that *outrageous* makes of the same gloss.

entries.definition: (used of opinions and actions) far beyond the norm
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A bare intensifier of position that shoves an opinion or action to the far edge and says nothing about it beyond how far out it sits.

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the excess for not being warranted rather than for its bulk, the quietest complaint among the words sharing its gloss.
examples: his dress stops just short of undue elegance

entries.definition: beyond normal limits
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Convicts the overstepping of having no argument for itself, a heavier charge than the plain over-the-limit of *excessive*.

entries.definition: befitting or characteristic of a young boy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Mildly fond, measuring against a young boy whether the thing suits one or simply resembles one.

entries.definition: very young
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and intensifying, pushing youth to its very beginning and saying how far along rather than how it looks.

entries.definition: including or intended for youthful persons
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely classificatory, sorting by who is taken in or aimed at, with none of the approval in *youthful*.

entries.definition: (of children and animals) young, immature
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmth sits in the diminutive: the child or young animal is made endearing, where *small* only measures.
examples: what a big little boy you are
Her little brother was not yet old enough for school.

entries.definition: (of children and animals) young, immature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Plain and unsentimental about the same young creature as *little*, sized rather than cherished.

entries.definition: young and immature
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Youth felt as softness, the immaturity something breakable rather than something admired.

entries.definition: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Literary and elevated where *young* and *youthful* are plain, admiring the vigour rather than merely reporting it.

entries.definition: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and direct, counting no years at all but the vigour and freshness that read as youth, and asserting it flatly where *youngish* hedges.
examples: he is young for his age
At sixty her step was still young.

entries.definition: somewhat young
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Hedged and faintly grudging, granting youth only approximately where *young* grants it outright.

entries.definition: suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts youth forward as a resemblance rather than a fact, so the freshness carries the whole of the claim.

entries.definition: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same desertion as *fail*, but framed as trust broken against the person left behind, which is why it is the heaviest word here.

entries.definition: fail to meet the hopes or expectations of
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest of the three: hopes or expectations simply come up short, with none of *fail*'s claim that someone was depended on and abandoned.
examples: Here are officers enough at Meryton to disappoint all the young ladies in the country.
Miss Bingley, however, was incapable of disappointing Mr. Darcy in anything

entries.definition: disappoint, prove undependable to; abandon, forsake
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on not being there when relied on, covering both the proving undependable and the walking away, but stated as a lapse rather than a wrong.
examples: Elizabeth's courage did not fail her.

entries.definition: lacking in power or forcefulness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the same want of power into a judgement — force was expected here and it is not there.

entries.definition: lacking in power or forcefulness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the missing power or forcefulness as a plain attribute, without the verdict *ineffectual* passes on it.
examples: like an unable phoenix in hot ashes
His unable protests did nothing to stop the sale.

entries.definition: marked by depth of thinking
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain, unshowy praise that locates the depth in the thinking itself rather than in the person's habit of it, as *thoughtful* does.
examples: For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books
